_comment: I0 provider playbook (schema: app/domain/playbook.py). Public facts only, every claim sourced. Coinbase's help and legal pages refuse automated fetches (HTTP 403): their wording comes from search snippets, so official claims are at most medium confidence. Criminal process goes through Coinbase's Kodex portal (LE officers only); civil process goes to its registered agent; victims can only report (Scam Hub for customers, the security inbox for phishing) and file IC3.
notes: Coinbase states no issuing jurisdiction: about half of its law-enforcement requests are non-US, and its international / EEA legal page has its own Kodex tenant. There is no public freeze-request procedure: freezes and seizures go through law enforcement process. The LE-questions inbox and the security inbox are not catalogued here (each address needs its own review).

entities.name: Coinbase international / EEA entities
entities.notes: The EEA legal page links its own Kodex sign-up; which entity holds a given account is not stated.

channels.label: Law-enforcement request portal (Kodex)
channels.notes: 'Subpoenas for criminal matters can be submitted by Law Enforcement Officers via our portal'; the officer creates an account first. Aegis never registers or submits there.

channels.label: Law-enforcement request portal, international / EEA (Kodex)
channels.notes: Linked from Coinbase's EEA legal page (search snippet; the page refused a direct fetch).

channels.label: Law-enforcement questions inbox
channels.notes: Coinbase names a subpoenas inbox on coinbase.com for other questions from law enforcement (and help with the portal goes to Kodex). For officers; not catalogued until reviewed.

channels.label: Registered Agent for Service of Process (civil matters)
channels.notes: Civil subpoenas and court papers are served on Coinbase's registered agent, not through the portal. Counsel looks up the current agent before service.

channels.label: Security inbox (phishing and scam-site reports)
channels.notes: Coinbase's help centre names a security inbox on coinbase.com for reporting phishing sites; signed-in customers use the in-app Scam Hub instead. Report only: no freeze is promised. Confirm the address before use.

coinbase.le.notes: Coinbase's LE channel is its Kodex portal (coinbase.kodex; international / EEA: coinbase.kodex_intl), for law enforcement officers only.

instrument.notes: An IC3 or police reference is recommended; Coinbase's help centre points victims to IC3.

paths.notes: Coinbase may flag addresses or restrict accounts internally; authorised transfers are treated as final and no freeze is guaranteed (secondary sources). Hand off to the case officer, who submits through Kodex.

instrument.notes: Subpoena, court order or search warrant matched to the record type.

paths.notes: Each request is reviewed; Coinbase may narrow over-broad requests or object to legally insufficient ones. Users are typically notified of legal process unless a non-disclosure order applies (secondary).

instrument.notes: No public freeze-request procedure; the instrument depends on the jurisdiction.

paths.notes: Coinbase says it supported freezes in multi-agency scam operations; how a single freeze request is handled is not published.
US seizure warrant per secondary (law-firm) sources.

instrument.notes: A civil subpoena or court order served on the registered agent.
